title: Hormuz Traffic Near Total Collapse — 3-5 Ships Cross All Weekend vs. 130/Day Pre-War — as Oil Rises 2.7%
detail: CENTCOM said its forces have redirected 64 commercial vessels, disabled 3, and boarded 2 'to ensure compliance' since the US naval blockade of Iran was reimposed in mid-July — up from 44 redirected as of Aug 3. MarineTraffic data showed only 3-5 commercial ships transited the Strait of Hormuz over the Aug 15-17 weekend, against a pre-war average of roughly 110-130 vessels a day. Brent crude rose 2.7% to $90.87/bbl amid the standoff, as the 60-day US-Iran MOU deadline lapsed without a deal and Iran signaled a shift to a 'fully offensive' posture in the strait.

media.caption: Commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has collapsed to a handful of ships a day under the US blockade

title: Chief Engineer Killed as Unknown Projectile Strikes Bulker Minoan Dignity Exiting Strait of Hormuz
detail: The Liberia-flagged, Greek-managed bulk carrier Minoan Dignity (76,800 dwt, built 2004) was struck by an unknown projectile overnight between Aug 17 and 18 while transiting outbound through the Strait of Hormuz's southern corridor, about 0.5 nautical miles off the Omani coast. The projectile hit the starboard side and entered the engine room, killing the ship's chief engineer; two evacuation attempts were unsuccessful before the Omani Coast Guard responded. The vessel's Company Security Officer reported the incident at 01:35 UTC on Aug 18. UKMTO said no environmental impact had been reported and that authorities were investigating responsibility; no government or armed group had claimed the strike as of Aug 19. It was the second strike this month on a vessel under the same commercial management, following the Minoan Pioneer on Aug 4 — both ships had called at Bandar Imam Khomeini before being hit.

media.caption: The bulk carrier Minoan Dignity was struck in the engine room while exiting the Strait of Hormuz, killing the chief engineer

confidenceReason: No government or armed group has claimed responsibility; UKMTO and Omani authorities are still investigating the source of the projectile.

title: UAE Air Defenses Sound Nationwide Alert After Two Iranian Ballistic Missiles Fired Toward Emirati Waters
detail: The UAE Ministry of Defence said its air defense systems detected and responded to two Iranian ballistic missiles on the evening of Aug 18 — the first such alert since mid-July. A phone alert was sent to residents, mostly in Dubai and Sharjah, at 18:52 local time, with an all-clear issued roughly ten minutes later. One projectile landed in Emirati territorial waters; the second landed outside UAE territory. No casualties or ground damage were reported. The Ministry said it 'remained on high alert and fully prepared to deal with any threat.' Iran denied launching the missiles, calling the allegation baseless and describing it as a possible false-flag operation.
